messages:
sam: Heads up — hosted-eus3 GPU pool is showing sustained admission-control alerts since 11:12 UTC. p95 queue latency up to ~8s, inflight backlog >200 for last 20m. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/eus3/pool/gpu-backlog :rotating_light:

irene: seeing it too. spike aligns with a bulk onboarding job from tenant `acme-bulk` (lots of parallel small reqs). traffic rate jumped ~4x at 11:10. admission-controller logs show repeated rejections.

vikram: CPU on the node-manager hosts is fine but GPU allocation failed to scale — cloud quota refused new instances (quota: GPUs-per-region hit). also ~12% preemptible evictions reported which is amplifying churn.

opsbot: [alert] AdmissionControlThrottle for pool hosted-eus3 triggered at 2026-03-18T11:12:08Z. drop_rate_p95=0.22, queue_depth=214, avg_tokens_per_request=18.

clare: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) enable temporary tenant-level soft-rate-limit for acme-bulk (throttle parallelism) 2) route heavy bulk requests to fallback smaller model (gpt-medium-quant) 3) trigger manual capacity bump (add 6 GPUs) while we sort quota. any objections? :thinking_face:

maya: +1 to all. I already opened cloud support ticket for quota increase (case #CS-4491). ETA for quota change unknown.

sam: I'll implement a short-lived per-tenant throttle. plan: set concurrency cap to 32 for acme-bulk and reduce max tokens to 512 for 20m window. command:```
# set tenant throttle
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/internal/routing/throttle -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL" -d '{"tenant":"acme-bulk","concurrency":32,"window_mins":20}'
```

irene: also pushing a routing rule to prefer eu-central as overflow for low-latency-tolerant requests. snippet:```
# routing patch
PATCH /internal/routing/policy/hosted-eus3
payload: {"overflow_regions":["eu-central"],"policy":"prefer_overflow","criteria":{"max_cost_ms":200}}
```

vikram: FYI we should also adjust autoscaler cooldown and headroom: current headroom 0.12 is too conservative for onboarding bursts. propose temp headroom=0.25 and allow autoscaler to provision spot+on-demand mix.

clare: agree. I'm updating the dashboard to surface quota errors and preemptible-eviction-rate as first-class metrics so on-call doesn't misinterpret CPU-only pressure.

opsbot: [info] Manual capacity bump requested by sam: +6 GPUs in hosted-eus3. cloud request id: req-9923.

maya: quick cost note — if we keep extra 6 GPUs on for 2 hours expect ~$540 extra. logging it in the incident budget.

sam: rollout timeline — applying throttle now, routing change in 2m, manual bump pending cloud. I'll post an update in 5m with queue impact. please watch the backlog panel (Queue depth / admission rejects).

clare: also tagging product-dev to ask acme-bulk to throttle their client-side parallelism on next deploy. @product-dev please echo to customer.

vikram: after throttle applied, backlog dropped ~40% within 90s. still watching p95. good quick win.

sam: thanks all. follow-up: create postmortem if ticket remains open >24h. we'll reconvene if eviction rate rises or quota doesn't clear. :white_check_mark:
